discovery: Spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots: proposal and experimental realization of coherent control of single electron spins

nominees.name: Charles M. Marcus
nominees.affiliation: University of Washington, USA, and Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, Denmark

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech and Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

subfield: Condensed matter physics / mesoscopic physics and quantum information
motivation: In 1998 Daniel Loss proposed using the spin of a single electron confined in a gate-defined semiconductor quantum dot as a qubit. Exchange coupling between neighbouring dots would provide the two-qubit gates. Experiments turned this idea into reality. Charles Marcus's group demonstrated coherent control and spin-echo recovery of two-electron singlet–triplet states in double dots, which exposed and then tamed hyperfine decoherence. Lieven Vandersypen's group achieved single-shot spin readout, driven coherent rotations of a single electron spin and, later, high-fidelity universal gates in silicon. Together these advances made Coulomb blockade and Pauli spin blockade, two subtle mesoscopic effects, into tools for controlling individual quantum states in a solid. They also opened a qubit platform that is compatible with semiconductor fabrication and is now pursued worldwide, including at industrial scale.
